inputs.text:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: final industrial-design presentation, one single coherent image file
Primary request: Create one polished, buildable product-design presentation of the resolved SHR-DAW Raspberry Pi 5 music workstation enclosure. This is the only concept image, not a page of alternate concepts.
Scene/backdrop: neutral warm-light-gray studio background, restrained industrial-design presentation board.
Subject: compact wedge-shaped desktop console, approximately 212 mm wide × 155 mm deep × 103 mm rear height. A 7-inch landscape touchscreen is flush in the sloping top, screen plane about 24 degrees above horizontal and facing the seated operator. Low front edge has a wide horizontal dark grille with fine vertical slots; immediately beneath/alongside it is a restrained row of exactly five small square off-white controller buttons and one tiny amber status light, no knobs. Rear shell drops vertically to the table to level the tilted body and forms a stable rear foot/plinth. Two discreet black silicone front feet.
Materials/textures: bead-blasted warm graphite powder-coated folded aluminum chassis and bottom plate, satin black PC-ABS display bezel, precise seams, captive screws, small warm-gray legend strip with no readable button labels. Coherent compact modern digital console with a subtle vintage amplified-console character, functional rather than decorative.
Composition/framing: one dominant front-right three-quarter product view large enough to clearly show the sloped screen, front intake grille, five buttons, and the right-side direct-access connector well containing four USB-A ports and one Ethernet jack. Add two smaller integrated inset views on the same board: (1) rear three-quarter view showing one and only one 40 mm square exhaust fan behind a high-open-area grille, a recessed rear-high cable bay containing exactly one USB-C power port and exactly two micro-HDMI ports, and the rear leveling foot; (2) clean side cutaway showing the truthful stack from top to bottom: display panel, upper airflow gap, Raspberry Pi 5 with active cooler facing upward into that gap, Raspberry Pi board, bottom-mounted NVMe base and SSD near an aluminum bottom plate. Use subtle unlabeled airflow arrows from front grille straight through the display/Pi gap to the rear exhaust, plus a smaller lower branch over the NVMe.
Screen content: a dark landscape terminal-style music workstation UI, dense but plausible 40-column by 13-row tracker/menu character, cyan/amber/soft-gray accents, small abstract meters and tracker columns; only the product name “SHR-DAW” may be legible, no other readable UI labels.
Lighting/mood: premium studio product rendering, soft key light, realistic shadows, sharp manufacturable edges, honest scale and connector geometry.
Constraints: one image file; one resolved product only; exactly one rear exhaust fan; exactly five front controller buttons; one native USB-C power port and two micro-HDMI ports together in the recessed rear-high bay; four USB-A plus Ethernet on the right side; no second USB-C; no audio jack; no impossible floating ports; no blocked grilles; no cable plugged in; no exposed bare PCB in the exterior views; side cutaway may reveal components; rear exhaust separated from front intake; display remains landscape and is not flipped; no branding except SHR-DAW; no dimension text, callout labels, watermark, hands, people, headphones, speakers, or decorative fake meters.
